municipality: Kuchi Gaon, Ward # 4, Kalikasthan, Panchadewal Binayak
description_en: Kuci Bihāra, built in 1354 CE and located in the village of Kuci, is a rectangular stone reservoir with three small arched passages leading inside the reservoir's small room. Water is delivered to the south-western wall of the room via a small stone pipe. The room has a corbelled ceiling with a rosette carved in the centre, and the main arch faces north-east. Other two arches are on the south-east and north-west sides of the building. The reservoir is capped by astūpa, with one central niche on each of its four sides.Each niche, with the exception of the one in the southwest, is filled with a vertical stone slab. Two of them still have Avalokiteśvara's mantra "oṃmaṇi padme hūṃ" written in Rañjanā script. A row of decorativeāmalakamotifs runs along the mid-height of thestūpa's four façades. The dome is topped by amaṇḍala-shaped slab and a five-levelchatra(umbrella).An inscription in Nāgarī script is found above the lintel of the north-eastern door. The text used to run the entire length of the façade. Some restoration work done around 2017 CE resulted in the misplacement of a stone block containing the end of the inscription, which is now up-side-down on the north-western side of the building. The inscription records a dedication in the year ŚS 1276 (1354CE) by Devavarmā, the Great Minister (mahāmātya) of King Pṛthvīmalla. Devavarmā is the same individual who constructed a large reservoir in Dullu the same year.The Dullu reservoir, also known as Patharnauli, is topped by astūpa, though it must have originally held five (Andolfatto 2019, p. 96; Pant 2009, 301). Only the Dullu and Kucistūpas' domes are comparable.The monument and its inscription were first mentioned by Yogi Naraharinath in 1956 CE (Naraharinath 1956: 45), and Prayag Raj Sharma in 1972 CE (Sharma 1972: 28). References include Tucci 1956: 46, Pant 2009: 302, Sharma 2012: 230-231, and Andolfatto 2019: 95-99. A new fountain was installed to the north-east of this mediaeval monument in 2017 CE.

historical_events.event_description: On the north-eastern side of the reservoir, above the main door's lintel, there is an inscription in Nāgarī script. The inscription is missing the right side. It is housed in a block on the structure's northwestern side.The inscription's text is as follows:śrīsake || śrīrājādhirājāpṛthvīmallaś ciraṃ jayatu || śrīdevavarmajayapuṇyena sarve satvā sukhino bhavaṃtuPant 2009 published an English translation:"In the glorious [year of] Śake 1276. May the glorious supreme king of kings Pṛthvīmalla long be victorious. May all beings be happy through the glorious Davarmā's victory [and] merit"

The mantra of Avalokiteśvara,oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ, is inscribed in Rañjanā script on the slabs in the upper niches of the building. Only the south-west side lacks an inscribed slab. On the south-western side, the mantra is most visible. The inscriptions must be from the time the monument was built, which was 1354 CE. The same mantra is also inscribed in Rañjanā script on other monuments dating from the mid-1350s.
